question:
A 4-year-old boy is brought to the physician because of swelling around his eyes for 4 days. The swelling is most severe in the morning and milder by bedtime. Ten days ago, he had a sore throat that resolved spontaneously. His temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 103/min, and blood pressure is 88/52 mm Hg. Examination shows 3+ pitting edema of the lower extremities and periorbital edema. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 15.3 g/dL
Leukocyte count 10,500/mm3
Platelet count 480,000/mm3
Serum
Urea nitrogen 36 mg/dL
Glucose 67 mg/dL
Creatinine 0.8 mg/dL
Albumin 2.6 mg/dL
Urine
Blood negative
Glucose negative
Protein 4+
RBC none
WBC 0–1/hpf
Fatty casts numerous
Protein/creatinine ratio 6.8 (N ≤0.2)
Serum complement concentrations are within the reference ranges. Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?"?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "4-year-old boy with periorbital edema" -> "edema suggests possible nephrotic syndrome" -> "urine shows 4+ protein" -> "low serum albumin indicates protein loss" -> "fatty casts suggest significant proteinuria" -> "serum complement levels normal" -> "likely minimal change disease" -> "prednisone is first-line treatment" -> 95%

CHAIN: "4-year-old boy with swelling around eyes" -> "recent sore throat may indicate post-infectious process" -> "edema is worse in the morning" -> "3+ pitting edema and periorbital edema present" -> "urine analysis shows significant proteinuria" -> "low serum albumin indicates nephrotic syndrome" -> "normal complement levels suggest minimal change disease" -> "prednisone is appropriate management" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Child presents with edema and recent sore throat" -> "edema is consistent with nephrotic syndrome" -> "urine shows high protein levels" -> "serum albumin is low" -> "fatty casts present in urine" -> "normal complement levels" -> "indicates minimal change disease" -> "prednisone is standard treatment" -> 85%

CHAIN: "4-year-old boy with periorbital and lower extremity edema" -> "recent history of sore throat" -> "edema pattern suggests nephrotic syndrome" -> "urine analysis shows significant protein" -> "low serum albumin confirms protein loss" -> "fatty casts indicate nephrotic syndrome" -> "normal complement levels" -> "prednisone is indicated" -> 90%
analysis: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings suggest that the child is experiencing nephrotic syndrome, likely due to minimal change disease, which is common in this age group. The key features include significant proteinuria (4+), hypoalbuminemia (2.6 g/dL), and edema. Given the diagnosis, the most appropriate next step in management is to initiate corticosteroid therapy, specifically prednisone, as it is the first-line treatment for nephrotic syndrome in children.
